title: Brown rice with dark green vegetables, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is a whole‑grain product obtained from the whole rice kernel after removing only the outer husk. The dish includes dark green vegetables (such as broccoli, spinach, green peas) and is prepared without added fat, making it low‑calorie and nutrient‑dense.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains the bran and germ, so it contains more fiber, vitamins, and minerals than white rice.
Dark green vegetables are rich in chlorophyll, giving them their characteristic color and antioxidant properties.
Because no fat is added, the dish is low in calories while still providing satiety through fiber and protein.
Brown rice has a lower glycemic index than white rice, helping to stabilize blood sugar levels.
When stored properly, whole brown rice can stay fresh for up to 6 months.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes a feeling of fullness, and helps maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Source of magnesium and selenium
items.content: These minerals are essential for muscle function, nervous system health, and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is important for amino‑acid metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Helps control blood glucose, beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Antioxidants from green vegetables
items.content: Lutein, zeaxanthin and other phytochemicals protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid in whole grains can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or sprouting the rice can mitigate this.

items.title: Arsenic in rice
items.content: Rice may contain trace amounts of arsenic; choose reputable brands and vary grains in the diet.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: Rare but possible; individuals with a rice allergy should avoid the product.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish as a standalone meal or as a side. It pairs well with lean protein such as grilled chicken, fish, or tofu, and can be added to salads. Cook the rice by steaming, add the vegetables at the end of cooking to keep them crisp and vibrant.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry brown rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked portions should be kept in the refrigerator for no more than 3‑4 days and reheated thoroughly before serving.
